records.name: Meta-Psychology
records.publisher: Linnaeus University Press; owned by the journal's editorial board
records.scope_notes: Metascience, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, reanalyses, replicability studies, statistical tutorials and research software with a clear contribution to psychological science. Requires a public preprint and open review workflow; data, code and materials are expected, with exceptional restrictions requiring editorial consideration. Statistical analyses undergo a reproduction check. General empirical psychology without a metascientific contribution is not automatically in scope.

route.conditions: The journal calls itself a completely free diamond open-access journal and excludes publishing fees. A separate explicit statement ruling out submission charges was not found in this pass, so the full zero-cost route remains conservatively unverified. Authors participate in formatting/copyediting; transparent review and public cover-letter requirements apply.
route.other_mandatory_costs: No required payment found; comprehensive submission-stage fee exclusion remains unconfirmed.

fee_evidence.note: Official journal describes diamond open access and no publishing fee; it does not separately itemize submission charges.
Submission workflow requires a preprint, submission form and linked materials; no payment requirement is listed. Absence alone does not verify all submission costs.

difficulty.basis: No acceptance probability or difficulty ranking established in this expansion pass.

records.name: Methodology: European Journal of Research Methods for the Behavioral and Social Sciences
records.publisher: PsychOpen GOLD / Leibniz Institute for Psychology (ZPID), for the European Association of Methodology
records.scope_notes: Statistical modeling, psychometrics, survey methodology, research design, methodological comparisons and instructional articles using real or simulated data and software. Current scope excludes applied/substantive papers, scale validation without a methodological contribution, and philosophical/theoretical essays. Existing-data studies must contribute to methodology rather than merely apply established sophisticated techniques.

route.conditions: Current journal homepage explicitly makes submission, review and publication free. Follow the 6000-word all-inclusive limit and six-figure maximum. PsychOpen GOLD announces closure by 31 December 2027. Recheck the journal's submission status, publisher and fees through the transition.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated for standard compliant articles; publisher policy says the entire process is free.

fee_evidence.note: Journal-specific homepage explicitly excludes submission, review and publication charges and identifies its PsychOpen GOLD partnership.
Publisher FAQ excludes submission and publication fees for all its journals and says the entire process is free.

records.name: Social Psychological Bulletin
records.publisher: PsychOpen GOLD / Leibniz Institute for Psychology (ZPID)
records.scope_notes: Basic and applied social psychology, theoretical reviews, evidence synthesis, methodological articles and empirical work. Secondary-data or computational work needs a substantive social-psychology contribution. Material AI policy: original text written by AI is prohibited even with disclosure; AI editing/translation is permitted with disclosure. People directing Agentic-Powered-Research must assess their actual workflow against that policy.

route.conditions: Journal excludes author fees and publisher FAQ explicitly excludes submission/publication fees. Respect article-type limits. Registered Reports use the PCI RR track and an annual publication quota. PsychOpen GOLD announces closure by 31 December 2027. Recheck the journal's submission status, publisher and fees through the transition.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated for standard compliant publication; no mandatory membership is specified.

records.name: Quantitative and Computational Methods in Behavioral Sciences
records.publisher: PsychOpen GOLD / Leibniz Institute for Psychology (ZPID)
records.scope_notes: Mathematical foundations, algorithms, simulation comparisons, statistical learning and software for behavioral-science methods. Method dissemination includes applied tutorials and new data tools. This is a methodological-contribution route rather than a general empirical outlet. Manuscripts become public preprints once review begins, including subsequently rejected work.

route.conditions: Journal explicitly excludes review/publication fees; PsychOpen's applicable platform policy also excludes submission fees. Public-preprint workflow and author formatting requirements apply. PsychOpen GOLD announces closure by 31 December 2027. Recheck the journal's submission status, publisher and fees through the transition.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated; publisher policy describes an entirely free process.

records.name: Psychological Thought
records.publisher: University Publishing House Neofit Rilski, South-West University, Blagoevgrad, Bulgaria
records.scope_notes: Broad psychological theory and empirical research, explicitly including meta-analyses; suitable nonclinical synthesis and justified secondary analyses can fit. English and Bulgarian are accepted. Although clinical reports and case studies are within the journal's wider remit, those formats do not establish an OSRI clinical-practice research route.

route.conditions: Current journal policy explicitly excludes submission and publication author fees. Manuscripts must meet the 35-page limit, Word/template requirements and anonymous review rules. Its preprint policy and anonymity wording are not fully aligned; verify compatibility before publicly identifying a submission.
route.other_mandatory_costs: None stated for standard compliant papers; no compulsory membership payment is specified.

fee_evidence.note: Current journal policy explicitly excludes author fees for submission and publication and identifies the university publisher since January 2020.

notes: Five additional journals, with no duplicate IDs or venues from discovery. Four have verified free submission/publication routes; Meta-Psychology remains conservatively needs_verification because a separate submission-fee exclusion was not established.

PsychOpen GOLD announces discontinuation by 31 December 2027. All three current PsychOpen candidates carry a transition caveat. Psychological Thought left PsychOpen in 2020 and is verified against its current university-hosted policy, not historical platform assumptions. Source: https://psychopen.eu/ ; https://psyct.swu.bg/index.php/psyct/about .

Excluded active-opportunity leads: Journal of Numerical Cognition currently pauses submissions during a publisher move (https://jnc.psychopen.eu/). Europe's Journal of Psychology paused new submissions on 18 February 2026 until further notice (https://ejop.psychopen.eu/). Journal of Social and Political Psychology has paused new submissions since 4 May 2026 and announces a move to Universidad de O'Higgins with reopening planned early in 2027, not yet established as reopened (https://jspp.psychopen.eu/).
Judgment and Decision Making is already in discovery and was not duplicated or treated as diamond.

Social Psychological Bulletin's AI-authorship and original-text restriction is material to Agentic-Powered-Research. Its fee-free status does not establish workflow compatibility. Official policy: https://spb.psychopen.eu/index.php/spb/author-policies .

QCMB official pages support peer review but differ on the reviewer minimum: its review page says at least two, while author instructions allow a minimum of one independent reviewer. Only the peer_reviewed label is asserted. Its homepage showed recent articles only through December 2024 and a 2025 volume link; no active manuscript submission was attempted. Sources: https://qcmb.psychopen.eu/index.php/qcmb/peer-review ; https://qcmb.psychopen.eu/index.php/qcmb/author-guidelines ; https://qcmb.psychopen.eu/ .

Scope fit is an agent interpretation of official scope and article-type policies. No new physical laboratory experiments or clinical practice are proposed. Manuscript-specific suitability, ethics, data reuse permissions, AI disclosure and final acceptance remain separate checks.
